source: genEd: almabot-web/src/lib/gened.ts (GENED), matched against the catalog's 'Degree Attributes' column. majors: ingest/majors.json, hand-transcribed from the catalog.illinois.edu program page each one names

majors.label: Computer Science, BS
aliases: bachelor of science in computer science

groups.label: Campus General Education requirements
groups.note: The program follows the campus Gen Ed requirements; required courses cover some of them (PHYS 211 and PHYS 212 for Natural Sciences & Technology, and MATH 220 or MATH 221, MATH 231, MATH 241, PHYS 211, PHYS 212, CS 124, CS 128, CS 225 for Quantitative Reasoning). Ask this tool for 'gened' with the same transcript to audit that half.

groups.label: Language other than English, third semester
groups.note: Completion of the third semester or equivalent of a language other than English, worth 0-15 hours depending on placement. Placement level and transfer credit decide it, and neither is a course code.

groups.label: Engineering orientation seminar
groups.note: ENG 100; external transfer students take ENG 300 instead.

groups.label: Calculus I
groups.note: MATH 220 may be substituted for MATH 221; 4 of its 5 credit hours count toward the degree.

groups.label: University physics: mechanics, and electricity & magnetism
Science elective, 3 hours
groups.note: One course from the Natural Science & Technology list beyond those used for General Education, and allowed for credit by The Grainger College of Engineering. ASTR 100, PHYS 101, PHYS 102 and CHEM 101 are excluded. The approved list is not part of this catalog export, so which course qualifies cannot be decided here.

groups.label: Six technical electives
groups.note: Six additional CS courses, chosen from CS 397 and the CS 400-level courses other than CS 400, CS 401, CS 402, CS 403 and CS 491. CS 421 is excluded here as well because the technical core already requires it and a course counts once. Three parts of this requirement are not checked: the 18 cumulative credit hours (a transcript of codes carries no hours), the six-hour cap on CS 397 and CS 499 together, and the CS Academic Office permissions that let a CS 500-level course or one 'CS-like' course in another department count.

groups.label: One technical elective from the team project list
groups.note: The team project course is one of the six technical electives, not a seventh course. CS 425 counts only in its 4-hour section, which a course code cannot distinguish.

groups.label: Three technical electives from a single focus area
groups.note: Eight focus areas, each a list of CS courses on the program page; the team project course may be one of the three. CS 498 and CS 598 sections may be added to a focus area by department approval, so the lists are not fixed and the choice of area is the student's.

groups.label: Free electives, 24-25 hours
groups.note: Whatever course work brings the degree to 128 hours, subject to The Grainger College of Engineering's restrictions on free electives.

groups.label: 40 hours of upper-division course work
groups.note: A university requirement, generally 300- and 400-level, drawn from every part of the degree. It is an hour total, and hours are not in this data.

groups.label: Technical GPA of at least 2.0
groups.note: Over the CS and MATH courses. Grades are not part of a transcript of course codes.

groups.label: 128 hours to graduate
groups.note: The degree total. Counting it needs credit hours for every course the student has taken, including those this one-term catalog does not list.

groups.label: Campus General Education requirements
groups.note: The program follows the campus Gen Ed requirements; required courses cover some of them (MATH 241, and STAT 107 or STAT 200 or STAT 212, for Quantitative Reasoning). Ask this tool for 'gened' with the same transcript to audit that half.

groups.label: Language other than English, fourth semester
groups.note: The fourth semester or equivalent of one language other than English, or the third semester of two different languages, worth 0-20 hours depending on placement.

groups.label: Calculus I
groups.note: The calculus sequence through MATH 241 is 11-12 hours; MATH 220 is the five-hour entry into it.

groups.label: Four advanced statistics electives, 12 hours
groups.note: The catalog lists MATH 444 and MATH 447 as one option between them ('MATH 444 or MATH 447'), so a student who took both is credited twice here and should not be: four distinct rows of the list are what the requirement asks for.

groups.label: 70-72 hours of major and supporting course work
groups.note: The hour total the course lists above normally come to. Hours are not in this data.

groups.label: 12 hours of 300- and 400-level work in the major on this campus
groups.note: Where a course was taken is not a course code, so this cannot be checked from a transcript of codes.

groups.label: 40 hours of upper-division course work
groups.note: A university requirement, generally 300- and 400-level, drawn from every part of the degree.

groups.label: 120 hours to graduate
groups.note: The degree total. Counting it needs credit hours for every course the student has taken, including those this one-term catalog does not list.

notes.majors: Major and degree requirements are not present in course-catalog.csv, which lists sections only. The programs in `majors` were transcribed by hand from the catalog.illinois.edu program pages each one names, for the catalog year in force for this term; they are two of the roughly 250 the campus offers. Requirements a course list cannot decide -- credit hours, GPA, placement, approved lists -- are marked kind 'advising' and are never counted as met.
notes.culturalStudies: Each campus Gen Ed category needs at least one course; Cultural Studies needs all three of cultwest / cultnonwest / cultus. Satisfying all 13 categories listed here covers the campus requirement.
